hero.title: The Neotia University
hero.summary: At Sarisa in West Bengal, The Neotia University brings crop science, laboratory work and rural learning together through its School of Agriculture and Allied Sciences. Its four-year agriculture degree includes village attachment and agro-industrial experience, with teaching extending across soils, crops, plant protection, horticulture and farm economics.

overview.heading: Agriculture study near Diamond Harbour
paragraphs: TNU’s agriculture course connects crop science with work in farming environments. Its published curriculum includes soil science, horticulture, plant protection, genetics and agricultural economics. The degree page describes four years of study, with rural agricultural experience and an agro-industrial attachment in the final stage.

The school’s older official brochure describes teaching farms, laboratories and small production units, including mushroom and apiculture activity. Such settings connect scientific observation with day-to-day production decisions. The 2026–27 fee schedule identifies the agriculture bachelor’s degree alongside agribusiness, diploma and postgraduate routes, giving applicants distinct study options to compare.

programmes.name: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture
programmes.summary: A broad agriculture degree with a published final-semester rural and industrial attachment.
programmes.eligibility: Course page: 10+2 with at least 55% in Physics, Chemistry and Biology/Mathematics, or the stated agriculture/horticulture vocational combination; reconfirm for the applying year.
programmes.admission_route: University entrance test is stated on the course page.

fees.includes: Published semester course fee for Indian students.
fees.note: One-time fee ₹29,000; published course total ₹597,000. Confirm accommodation and any charges outside the listed course fee.

admissions.heading: Applying to TNU
admissions.intro: TNU publishes a central application process. The course page confirms a university entrance test; its mixed-year dates require a fresh intake notice before planning a deadline. The live site now advertises 2027–28 admissions; the sourced 2026–27 fees and process documents below must not be relabelled as the next intake’s terms.
eligibility_points: The published B.Sc. Agriculture threshold is 55% in the specified 10+2 subject combination.

steps.title: Start the university application
steps.text: Use the official admission process page and enter the Class 10 roll number correctly; the page identifies it as an application identifier.

steps.title: Confirm the intake notice
steps.text: Request the applicable entrance schedule and a dated fee statement for B.Sc. Agriculture.

campus.heading: Agricultural teaching and practical work
campus.intro: The course page identifies experimental fields, crop laboratories and farm machinery for teaching. The older school brochure additionally describes production demonstrations.

The older brochure describes compost, mushroom and beekeeping units.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: The approved 2026–27 fee schedule expressly excludes B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture from the university’s general 25–100% tuition-scholarship offer. Agriculture applicants should obtain written confirmation of any separate government or programme-specific support before using a scholarship in their budget.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: The university's NIRF 2025 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

statistics.label: UG four-year programmes: 2023-2024
statistics.value: 211 graduates in minimum stipulated time; 59 placed; 152 selected for higher studies; median annual salary of placed graduates ₹6,50,000.
statistics.reporting_source: NIRF 2025, Agriculture and Allied Sectors, institutional submission

statistics.label: PG two-year programmes: 2023-2024
statistics.value: 18 graduates in minimum stipulated time; 9 placed; 9 selected for higher studies; median annual salary of placed graduates ₹7,00,000.
statistics.reporting_source: NIRF 2025, Agriculture and Allied Sectors, institutional submission

faqs.question: Where is TNU’s teaching campus?
faqs.answer: The campus address published on the agriculture page is Sarisa on Diamond Harbour Road in South 24 Parganas.

faqs.question: Which TNU course is in this ICAR record?
faqs.answer: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture, with a register term of 20 June 2024 to 19 June 2029.

faqs.question: How long is the agriculture degree?
faqs.answer: The official course page describes a four-year programme.

faqs.question: Does the course include village work?
faqs.answer: Yes. The published final-stage curriculum includes a village attachment within rural agricultural work experience.

faqs.question: What are TNU’s published 2026–27 B.Sc. Agriculture fees?
faqs.answer: For Indian students, the official table lists ₹71,000 per semester plus ₹29,000 one time, with a published course total of ₹597,000. These figures describe the listed course charges; confirm accommodation separately.

faqs.question: Does ICAR listing cover TNU’s fisheries courses here?
faqs.answer: This audited TNU record names agriculture only. Fisheries accreditation cannot be inferred from this entry.

faqs.question: Are verified agriculture placement figures available?
faqs.answer: The NIRF 2025 agriculture/allied submission reports UG four-year programmes (2023-2024): 59 placed from 211 graduates in minimum time, with ₹6,50,000 median annual salary among those placed; PG two-year programmes (2023-2024): 9 placed from 18 graduates in minimum time, with ₹7,00,000 median annual salary among those placed. These are historical group-level outcomes, not specialisation-level placement promises.
